_about: The one place a game term gets its English name. Every keyword, zone, phase, resource, stat, card type and recurring card-text phrase gets an entry BEFORE it appears in code, UI or docs; tools/pirate-ship_cards.py fails on a card field whose term has no entry. For a non-English game 'source' is the printed term; for an English game it is the printed term too (the entry still fixes one spelling and one code). Card names are never translated. tools/pirate-ship_import.py writes files/pirate-ship/GLOSSARY.md from this file.
policy: Card names stay exactly as printed.
Brand words (the game's own coined names) are never translated.
Use the English term in every screen, log line, rule and message; show the original only in the rules help and the glossary.
A new term gets an entry here before it appears anywhere else.
One term, one code: code is the identifier used in JSON fields, enums and CSS classes.

terms.note: Stage 1: the view widens and fish show as silhouettes.
A fish seen under the water, within the fisher's visible range.
Stage 3: a moving line sweeps the cone; its stop sets the cast heading.
Stage 4: up-and-down meter; its target spot sets the cast distance.
Stage 5: pick a rhythm and play it to draw the fish.
A beat pattern the lure plays; each fish prefers one.
The float that waits, twitches and submerges during the bite.
A twitch of the bobber before the bite; striking on it is a miss.
A hook press during a nibble: the fish is lost.
Stage 6: the bobber submerges with a splash and a sound.
The press that sets the hook once the bobber submerges.
Time after the bite in which a press still hooks; grows with Reflexes.
Stage 7: reel the fish in against line tension.
Strain on the line; past the break threshold it snaps.
Remaining line strength during pull in; hard pulls past the weaken threshold drain it until the line snaps.
How far the fish must be drawn in during pull in; the HUD bar fills as pulls add progress.
